scope: Research/reconciliation only. No bus-stop Civic Map assets are added in this step.

controllingBaseline.source: Makati City Basic Facts and Figures 2023
controllingBaseline.sourceOffice: Department of Engineering and Public Works (DEPW)
controllingBaseline.geography: Present-day Makati; source says excluding the 10 transferred barangays

countHistory.geography: 33-barangay Makati before final boundary transfer implementation in city statistics

historicalInfrastructureLineage.source: City Government of Makati infrastructure inventory, 1986–2017
historicalInfrastructureLineage.finding: DEPW historically tracked 36 waiting sheds as other structures. The publication does not name the sheds and does not establish that waiting shed is equivalent to the later bus-stop metric.

regulatoryDefinitionContext.source: Makati City Ordinance 2019-A-102 — Environmental Health Code
regulatoryDefinitionContext.finding: The ordinance regulates bus/jeepney/PUV stops and sheds/waiting areas as separate terminal-related categories. This is another reason not to equate the historical waiting-shed count with the 2023 bus-stop count.

sourcesChecked: Makati physical/infrastructure profile and CLUP profile material
Makati procurement/indexed city records searched for bus stop, bus shed, waiting shed, loading/unloading and bus bay terminology
Current Makati repository data for previously sourced bus-stop inventories
currentNamedInventorySearch.note: The reviewed authoritative material publishes counts and regulatory categories but not a current named 32-stop roster with addresses/coordinates.

existingCivicMapCrosswalk.reason: No authoritative source reviewed establishes that the three EDSA Busway stations or One Ayala Terminal are members of DEPW's 32-stop inventory. They remain valid current supplemental transport assets, but are not used to reverse-engineer the city denominator.

reconciliationDecision.rule: Do not create any of the 32 DEPW bus-stop assets until a named current roster, geospatial layer, engineering schedule, or equivalent source-backed list is obtained.

anomalyAssessment.observation: The published count rises from 17 in 2022 to 32 in 2023 even though the 2023 city statistics exclude the 10 transferred barangays.
anomalyAssessment.interpretation: This indicates a likely inventory update, reclassification, data correction, or changed counting basis; the available sources do not explain which.
anomalyAssessment.guardrail: Do not infer that the 15-stop increase represents newly built stops, Busway stations, transferred-area adjustments, or waiting sheds without documentary evidence.

unresolvedEvidenceTargets: DEPW engineering or maintenance schedule listing the 32 stops
Public Safety Department / traffic-management loading-unloading zone inventory tied to bus stops
Current city transport plan appendix with stop-level names
